answer: Helium is a 7‑billion‑parameter text‑only language model that was pretrained on 2.1 trillion tokens of public English data. [1]

Inner Monologue is a training and inference setup for Moshi that decomposes speech into a chain of text, semantic and acoustic tokens and predicts this structured sequence in a hierarchical manner, allowing the model to represent all utterances as both text and speech rather than switching modalities [1][2]. By integrating acoustic tokens into the same generative model, Inner Monologue enables generating arbitrary voices and conditions instead of a single speaker, and it decomposes generation on a per‑frame basis so each prediction step outputs a speech frame, making Moshi compatible with real‑time generation [1]. This hierarchical modeling also avoids increasing the Transformer sequence length while still allowing the model to predict time‑aligned text tokens before audio tokens, which significantly improves the factuality and linguistic quality of generated speech and permits deriving streaming TTS and ASR systems from Moshi [1][2]. The method further allows controlling Moshi via the text stream, for example forcing the sampling of an EPAD token to make Moshi start talking immediately, thereby providing additional flexibility in dialogue control [3]. Overall, Inner Monologue is used to improve linguistic quality, enable real‑time full‑duplex dialogue, and provide a unified multimodal generation framework [1][4][2]

In practice, the design chooses Mamba‑2 layers as the primary building blocks for both encoder and decoder because they handle fine‑grained inputs effectively while offering substantial computational efficiency on long sequences [2]. This choice satisfies the dual objectives of the encoder—preserving fine‑grained detail for residual transmission and compressing inputs into richer chunks for the main network—and of the decoder—combining coarse‑grained representations from the main network with fine‑grained encoder residuals [2].
